title: CM-EVS: Sparse Panoramic RGB-D-Pose Data for Coverage-Oriented Scene Observation
claim: A greedy loop scores candidate views by new coverage minus conflict cost against accumulated geometry, then acquires the winner and updates the state.
layout: 3 numbered panels, left-to-right, with a feedback loop arrow and score formulas
description: A three-panel horizontal pipeline with numbered blue circles. Panel 1 shows a 3D indoor room mesh seen from above. It is dotted with blue accumulated points and ringed by green wireframe globes for the previously selected ERP views, joined by dashed lines. A legend sits at the bottom. Panel 2 evaluates a candidate view in three steps. The warped historical ERP is outlined in blue, the rendered probe in orange, and the per-pixel masks in green, blue and red. A downward arrow runs alongside, and a box below gives the gain, conflict and score formulas with λ=0.35. Panel 3 shows candidate globes with scores, and the winner v4 (0.64) is highlighted in green. Below that are a high-resolution panorama and a point-cloud update equation, C_t = C_{t-1} ∪ new points, with a green arrow looping back. The eye goes first to the room render and the panoramas.

abstract: Modern 3D visual learning relies on observations sampled from metric 3D assets, yet existing scans, meshes, point clouds, simulations, and reconstructions do not directly provide a sparse, comparable, and geometry-consistent panoramic training interface. Dense trajectories duplicate nearby views, source-specific rendering policies yield heterogeneous annotations, and sparse heuristics may miss important regions or introduce depth-inconsistent observations. We study how to convert 3D assets into compact panoramic RGB-D-pose data with candidate-observable coverage and auditable provenance. We propose COVER (Coverage-Oriented Viewpoint curation with ERP Range-depth warping), a training-free ERP viewpoint curator that projects geometry observed from selected views into candidate ERP probes, scores incremental coverage, and penalizes depth conflicts. Under bounded proxy error and score-matching conditions, its greedy coverage proxy preserves the standard coverage-style approximation behavior up to an additive error term. Using COVER, we build CM-EVS (Coverage-curated Metric ERP View Set), a panoramic RGB-D-pose dataset with 36,373 curated ERP frames from 1,275 indoor scenes across Blender indoor, HM3D, and ScanNet++, complemented by outdoor panoramas from TartanGround and OB3D re-encoded into the same schema. Each frame provides full-sphere RGB, metric range depth, calibrated pose; COVER-produced indoor frames include per-step provenance logs. With a median of only 25 frames per indoor scene, CM-EVS covers all 13 unified room types while maintaining compact scene-level coverage. Experiments show that COVER improves the evaluated coverage–task trade-off, making CM-EVS a sparse, compact, and auditable RGB-D-pose resource for geometry-consistent panoramic 3D learning.
